Variants.Content: House Whitehead is based in the Weeping Town and are Stormland nobles sworn to Storm's End. Weeping Town is located on the windy east coast. The port not only accepts fishing boats, merchant ships and travelers across the sea, but it must also beware of storms, pirates and sudden conquests. The importance of this family is not to boast of long-standing royal lineage, but to maintain the defense of docks, roads and coasts: to organize rescues when ships are wrecked, to light alarms when enemy sails appear, and to send troops when summoned by lords. Owners and flags may change with war, but Weeping Town's dependence on sea routes does not change.
Entry Whitehead Local families also rely on water, roads, arable land, herds, and markets where goods can be exchanged; if any road, well, or dock fails, the price falls first on them.

Entry Whitehead They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the known world; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but real distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Whitehead If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Whitehead A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Whitehead They care about water sources, roads, cultivated land, herds, and markets where goods can be exchanged. They also look at whether seeds are left after harvesting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
